questions.question: Your company uses GitHub Copilot Business. A repository named contoso-shop contains a folder named /config that holds sensitive configuration files. You need to prevent Copilot from using files in that folder for suggestions or as context. The solution must affect only this repository. What should you configure?

options.text: The github.copilot.enable setting in each developer's VS Code
options.why: This is a personal per-language setting. It does not target a folder and each developer can change it.

options.text: A content exclusion in the repository settings for the path /config/**
options.why: Correct. Repository-level content exclusions list paths that Copilot must not use in that repository.

options.text: The Suggestions matching public code policy set to Block
options.why: This policy controls matches with public code. It does not exclude files in your repository.

options.text: A .gitignore entry for the /config folder
options.why: .gitignore affects which files Git tracks. It is not a Copilot content exclusion.

questions.explanation: Repository settings › Copilot › Content exclusion lets a repository admin list paths for that repository only.

questions.question: An organization owner must exclude every .env file in all repositories in the organization from GitHub Copilot, including repositories created in the future. Which organization-level content exclusion meets the requirement?

options.why: Correct. The "*" key applies the listed paths to every repository in the organization.

options.text: contoso-shop: ["**/.env"]
options.why: This applies only to the contoso-shop repository.
The key must be a repository name or "*", and the list must contain paths. The structure is reversed.
This is the repository-level list format and matches only a .env file at the root.

questions.explanation: Organization exclusions use YAML that maps a repository name, or "*" for all repositories, to a list of paths.

questions.question: A file in a repository matches a content exclusion. Which TWO behaviors should a developer expect in a supported IDE? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Copilot does not provide inline suggestions while the developer edits the file
options.why: Correct. Excluded files receive no inline suggestions in supported IDEs.

options.text: The file is hidden from the editor's file explorer
options.why: Exclusions affect Copilot only. The file remains visible and editable.

options.text: Copilot does not use the file's content as context for suggestions in other files
options.why: Correct. Excluded content is not used as context.

options.text: The file is encrypted in the repository
options.why: Content exclusions do not encrypt or modify files.

questions.explanation: Excluded files give no inline suggestions and are not used as context in supported IDEs. The files themselves are unchanged.

questions.question: A developer on Copilot Business finds that inline suggestions are distracting when writing Markdown documentation. Suggestions must remain available in all other languages. The developer has no administrative rights. What should the developer do?

options.text: Ask the organization owner to add a content exclusion for **/*.md
options.why: This would affect every developer and is an administrative control for sensitive content, not a personal preference.

options.text: Uninstall the GitHub Copilot Chat extension
options.why: This removes Copilot for all languages.

options.text: Set markdown to false in the github.copilot.enable setting
options.why: Correct. github.copilot.enable turns completions on or off per language for the individual developer.

options.text: Set the Suggestions matching public code policy to Block
options.why: This policy does not disable suggestions for a language, and developers on organization seats cannot change it.

questions.explanation: The github.copilot.enable editor setting is the per-language personal switch for completions.

questions.question: A developer uses GitHub Copilot Pro on personal repositories and wants to configure content exclusions. What should you tell the developer?

options.text: Content exclusions are configured in the developer's personal Copilot settings.
options.why: Personal settings do not include content exclusions.

options.text: Content exclusions require a .github/copilot-instructions.md file.
options.why: Custom instructions guide responses. They do not exclude content.

options.text: Content exclusions are available only on Copilot Free.
options.why: Copilot Free does not include content exclusions.

options.text: Content exclusions are available for Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise, not for individual plans.
options.why: Correct. Content exclusion is a Business and Enterprise feature.

questions.explanation: Content exclusions are configured by repository, organization or enterprise admins and require Copilot Business or Enterprise.
